result.result:
`{% set %}` now accepts namespace attributes in multi-variable assignments, such as `{% set full.prev_id, full.id = full.id, full.id + "/" + id %}`. The full test suite passes (909 tests). Running the issue's loop now gives `a/b a/b/c` instead of the syntax error.

**Root cause:** the parser only recognised a namespace attribute (`name.attr`) when it was the whole target. For a target with commas, it took a general path that didn't recognise namespace attributes, so it stopped at the first comma with `expected token 'end of statement block', got ','`.

**Changes:**
- **`src/jinja2/parser.py`:** a new helper, `_parse_namespace_target`, reads `name.attr` as a namespace reference and anything else as before. `parse_assign_target` uses it for single targets, and `parse_tuple` has a new `with_namespace` flag that uses it for each item. Only `{% set %}` turns this on; `for` loops are unchanged.
- **`src/jinja2/compiler.py`:** the check that the object really is a namespace used to be written in the middle of the generated assignment line. That breaks once the attribute sits inside a tuple, so a new `write_ns_checks` writes a check for every namespace attribute in the target before the assignment line. It covers both `{% set %}` and block `{% set %}…{% endset %}`, and `visit_NSRef` now writes only `ref[attr]`.
- **`tests/test_core_tags.py`:** three new tests:
  - swapping two namespace attributes;
  - mixing a plain variable with a namespace attribute (`{% set x, ns.b = 1, 2 %}`);
  - checking that a non-namespace object in a tuple target still raises `TemplateRuntimeError`.
- **`CHANGES.rst`:** a changelog entry under the unreleased version.

I also checked by hand that a single `{% set ns.a = 5 %}` and block `{% set ns.a %}…{% endset %}` still work. mypy isn't installed in the venv, so I didn't type-check the changes.

Parenthesised targets like `{% set (ns.a, b) = … %}` still give a syntax error, as before. Nothing is committed.
